Prevention: Take preventive actions in early spring before the rain season.
Plant trap crops (mung bean, broad bean, garden balsam) between cotton and kill bugs concentrated with insecticides (see yellow column).
Choose tolerant varieties with heavy hair, more oil glands, less bracts, less nectar glands, high tannin content (Arkot series).
Adopt tiny-stream furrow irrigation method to avoid moist environment that bugs like.
Avoid intercropping /adjacent- cropping with host crops (such as sunflower, date tree and alfalfa).
Plough weeds + crop residues to destroy overwintering sites.
Monitoring: Investigate the bug’s population every 7 days from early
Look for symptoms of tiny brownish dots on leaves, buds, flowers and cotton bolls at early damage stage.
If found look for the green <½ cm bugs.
In later damage stages, the black dots turn to irregular holes on leaves, cause the drop of buds, flowers and bolls and make the plant blistered and distorted.
Consider control action if 5-10 bugs are found on at least 3 out of 100 plants in the seedling and bud stages and 15-25 bugs on at least 10 out of 100 plants in the flower and boll maturation stages
Direct Control: Reduce the use of pesticides or choose relatively safe pesticides (e.g.
Lime sulphur) to protect natural enemies (such as parasitoids, ladybeetles, spiders).
Pull out seriously infested leaves or plants out of crops but leave behind ladybeetles, spiders.
Hang purple or cyan sticky boards above the crop (15 traps per ha) to trap and kill bugs.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides http:// www.chinapesticide.gov.cn/
